generatedProse.concept-context: Across the School of Sport, learning by doing takes several forms. Placements put you into clubs, schools and performance settings. Fieldwork takes you out to observe sport and activity in a community. Practical sessions let you coach or test in real time, and live projects, such as planning a session for a real squad, give you real work with real consequences. Each is a different shape of the same idea: you learn your sport subject by practising it.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two School of Sport students on a sport coaching pathway are each offered a piece of learning by doing.

Tom is told his activity is 'just a session plan' for a local junior squad, and assumes it does not really count, because it is not a proper placement at a professional club. He almost dismisses it, thinking practice- and work-based learning only means one thing.

Amara recognises her own task, coaching a real training session for a community team, as the same kind of learning in a different form. It is not a placement, but it is real coaching with real players and real consequences, so it is learning by doing, shaped to fit sport coaching.

Both were offered practice- and work-based learning. Only Amara saw that it comes in many forms, and that a session plan and a club placement both count.
generatedProse.summary: In the School of Sport, practice- and work-based learning takes many forms: club, school and performance placements, fieldwork, practical coaching and testing, and live projects. You can now recognise that range and give a sport example. What they share is learning by doing. The next lesson turns to why this kind of learning is so valuable to you.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara understand that Tom did not?

items.text: That coaching a real session is learning by doing, just in a different form from a placement.
That a placement at a professional club is the only real form of learning by doing.
That practice- and work-based learning only counts at a professional club.
That her session plan did not really count as learning.

feedback.correct: That's right. Coaching a real session is practice- and work-based learning in a different form from a placement.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara recognised about the different forms this learning can take.
